Author: M.S. Ramachandra Rao Bench: M.S. Ramachandra Rao

Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:3432 ) IN THE HIGH COURT OF HIMACHAL PRADESH,
SHIMLA LPA No. 237 of 2023 Date of decision : 13.6.2024.

.
 Suresh Kumar ...Appellant.
Versus  Zila Parishad, District Solan & another ...

Respondents  Coram:
The Hon'ble Mr. Justice M.S. Ramachandra Rao, Chief Justice.
The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Satyen Vaidya, Judge.
Whether approved for reporting?
For the appellant : Mr. P.D. Nanda, Advocate.
For the respondents : Mr. Surender Thakur, Advocate, for respondent no.1.
Mr. Govind Korla, Additional Advocate General, for respondent no.2.
Sh. Virender Sharma, Panchayat Secretary, District Panchayat Office, Solan is present in person.
M.S. Ramachandra Rao Chief Justice, (Oral):
This appeal is preferred by the appellant challenging the order dt. 29.12.2022 passed by the learned Single Judge in CWPOA No. 5478 of 2019.

sentences.text: Appellant was initially engaged as Panchayat Sahayak on part time basis on 12.10.1999, and he was later brought on fixed .
remuneration on the said post in the year 2007.
Thereafter, he was appointed as Panchayat Secretary on contract basis on 22.6.2009.

3. Since his services were not regularized, and he was being made to continue on contract basis,
which was later converted into temporary basis on 31.8.2015, the appellant had given a representation on 2.9.2015 to the respondents seeking regularization of his services.
4. When that was not decided, he filed O.A. no. 5788 of 2016 before the H.P. Administrative Tribunal.
5. The O.A. no. 5788 of 2016 was disposed of on 21.11.2016 by the Tribunal with a direction to the respondents to decide the same in accordance with law within one month.
6. Thereafter Annexure A-8 order dt. 19.12.2016 was issued by the Chief Executive Officer, Zila Parishad, Solan (1st respondent) stating

that the competent authority had considered his name for regularization of his service in August, 2015 but order in that regard was sealed due to case registered by the SV&AC of Himachal Pradesh Police, till the settlement of the said case.

7. No doubt, an FIR no. 13 of 2010 dt. 14.8.2010 was registered by the SV& AC, Solan, Himahal Pradesh under the .
provisions of Sections 420, 467, 468, 511 of IPC and Section 13 (2) of Prevention of Corruption Act,
1988, and it is also not in dispute that charge-sheet has been filed in the said case on 6.8.2019 naming the petitioner as accused person, but the case is still pending before the appropriate criminal Court and no final judgment has been pronounced.

8. When the petitioner approached this Court by filing CWPOA no. 5478 of 2019, this Court did not grant him any relief in the impugned order by observing that petitioner can approach the Court for redressal only in the event he is acquitted in the criminal case.

9. Counsel for the appellant contends that there is no provision in the rules dealing with the regularization of services to place in a sealed cover; that the sealed cover procedure would apply only in the case of promotion and has no application for regularization of service.
10. He also submits that both FIR and the charge-sheet contain only allegations against the appellant and till the appellant is convicted, there is presumption of innocence in his favour.

He further points out that though FIR was registered in the year 2010, it took nine years to file a charge-sheet on 6.8.2019, and it is not known .
when the criminal case is likely to be decided.

Suresh Kumar vs Zila Parishad on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61823795/
2 11.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar vs Zila Parishad on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for respondent no.2 is not able to show any provision of law which applies sealed cover procedure to cases of regularization of service of employees.

12. Obviously, there appears to be no objection of appellant working on contract basis for the last fifteen years without regularization, notwithstanding the registration of FIR against him, and also filing of the charge-sheet.

13. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the learned Single Judge is not correct in denying the relief to the appellant in the Writ Petition on the pretext that criminal case is still pending trial and his case for regularization can only be dealt with later.

14. We are in agreement with the contention of counsel for the appellant that if the respondents had no objection for the appellant working as Panchayat Secretary on contract basis from 2009, for the last fifteen years, they cannot also object to his regularization on the ground that criminal case is pending trial.

15. In any event, if the appellant is convicted in the criminal case, he would lose employment straightway under the applicable .
law.
16.

Therefore, the LPA is allowed; impugned order dt.
29.12.2022 passed in CWPOA no. 5478 of 2019 by the learned Single Judge is set aside; and the respondents are directed to regularize the services of the appellant to the post of Panchayat Secretary from 31.8.2015, the date when his juniors were regularized with all consequential benefits,
including arrears of pay with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till the date of payment.
Such payment shall be made within four months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
No order as to costs.
Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(M.S. Ramachandra Rao)
